html:
SMTO-LLM-0077 — The model server couldn't finish the model download or removal

GUID: 5d61b712-d6d8-52d4-89b7-3e88f0cd74d3
Slug: local-ai-pull-failed
Domain: LLM · Subsystem: local_ai

What happened

  • You asked to download or remove a model, and the model server said it couldn't do it. Part of a download may already be on the Gateway computer.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. In a new message, ask SMTO to list the installed models on that Gateway's local AI server. This shows whether the model is already there, partly there, or already removed.
  2. Check the model name, including any tag after a colon, against the name published by the model provider. A misspelled or unknown name is a common reason the server refuses the download.
  3. Ask the person who manages the Gateway computer to confirm it can reach the internet and to read the model server's log. The error alone does not establish whether the server, the network or the download site caused it.
  4. Once the problem is fixed and the list shows the model isn't already done, ask SMTO to download or remove it again. Checking first avoids repeating a change that already finished.

What success looks like

  • The installed-models list shows the model present after a download, or gone after a removal.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the model name, to the person who manages that Gateway computer. Don't delete model files by hand while the model server is running.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The provider rejected or reported failure for an explicit model operation (Ollama pull, remove or show returned a non-success status, or the pull stream reported an error); partial download files may remain.

What this means

  • The provider rejected or reported failure for an explicit model operation; its HTTP/progress response establishes a failure signal but not the absence of partial files. Local AI management belongs to the selected Gateway and accepted profile. Starting a runtime does not activate it for the controller; recorded execution and unknown-effect facts determine whether reconciliation is required.

Why this can happen

  • The provider rejected or reported failure for an explicit model operation; its HTTP/progress response establishes a failure signal but not the absence of partial files.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the model operation's status and installed-model inventory; distinguish provider rejection from an interrupted response classified as unknown outcome.

How to fix it

  • Read the provider's error in the Ollama log on the Gateway host (model name not found in the registry, registry unreachable, permission or storage problems), then run local_ai.models to see installed models and any partial state. Request a new pull or remove only after confirming the current inventory.
  • Repair the provider-reported problem, inspect partial state and request a new operation only after that reconciliation.

Retry and execution caution

  • Only after exact state reconciliation.

How to verify the fix

  • Provider inventory and the operation receipt establish the intended model state.

What not to do

  • Do not replay uncertain mutations or stop externally owned processes.

Technical notes

  • Local AI management belongs to the selected Gateway and accepted profile. Starting a runtime does not activate it for the controller; recorded execution and unknown-effect facts determine whether reconciliation is required.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
